headToHead.voiceVerdict: Big improvement on round 1: Dash now owns a shape, the live downward pivot (start, 'No,', revise lower, lock it in with a cheer), and eight of our twelve use it. Cover the names on Rooftop, Sorry/Agreed, Pancakes/Toast, nod, and Crumb's empty slot and nobody else in the cast could have said them. But the other half of his stage voice is the spin tag '[bad fact]! [restate]! That's [business word]!', and Brock does exactly that with gym words ('That's a PR!', 'That's not a record. That's a WARMUP.', 'Progress!'). Cover the jargon on 'Silver! Silver's a metal! I've never medalled!' or 'Great show! Everyone! I'm going to go stand very still somewhere!' and it is Brock. The roasts that clip best (lawsuits, ghosts) are clipped deadpan any suitor could deliver with the vocabulary swapped. Liam's formal-clause-on-trivia register holds in every line he has. Bar wins narrowly.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours wins on the twelve. The punch sits on the last word almost every time (market, nod, lawsuits, engaged, converts, dip, March), the pivots are real turns, and nothing in the twelve explains itself. Liam's set is looser: the time-machine line has no turn, the reported-speech line is a paraphrase, and three of the twelve are narrator lines doing the work for him. Across the whole bank the picture is worse (see the generic list), but on the best-twelve comparison construction goes to ours.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Tie. 'Pre-revenue, post-heartbreak, and open to acquisition', 'Second! Out of two! That's top two!' and 'You're the market!' are character portraits in one breath and would clip. Liam still has the two lines the fandom actually repeats ('Save me from the consequences of my actions!', the 360-degree spin), because his self-image is wrong in a way he cannot see. Dash now has a few lines of that kind; he does not yet have more of them.

That's demand!', 'That's three touchpoints!', 'That's three wows!', 'That's a subscription!', 'That's a strategy!', 'That's top two!', 'look at that re-engagement!', 'Silver's a metal!', 'Exclusive!' The ladder: a word repeated and escalated or downgraded three or four times (about 9 lines). 'Big fan, huge fan, okay, medium, growing', 'Not now is basically later! Later is basically soon!', 'Pivoting to friends! Pivoting to colleagues!', 'Rounding up! Rounding it up to a kiss!', 'Clip this! No, clip the next one!', 'Total stranger, total stranger... warm lead! ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. All 6 openers at 12 or under, all 10 jabs at 10 or under, three-words exactly 3, everything else at 20 or under ('That's the face! That's the face from the deck! Slide one! I drew it from memory and I nailed it!' sits exactly at 20). No em or en dashes, no emoji, no non-ASCII, no 'as an AI', no real people or brands, nothing past PG-13.
Stock romance filler, borderline: 'Some suitors bring roses, some bring a ring.' and 'Forever! Ish! Forever!' (the second earns it with 'Ish').

Inline lists, borderline against 'no lists': 'Married! Divorced! Remarried!', 'High intent, low patience, serious bounce risk.', 'Same me, gold border, ninety-nine a month.', 'Pivoting to friends! Pivoting to colleagues! Pivoting to someone you nod at!'.

Persona break on stage: 'High intent, low patience, serious bounce risk. Ninety seconds in and you've checked the exit twice.' The persona says he is the only one in the room who cannot see the zero; this line has him reading the star's boredom accurately.

Secret adjacency on stage: 'Off the record? Every night I say goodnight to my dashboard. It never says it back. Yet!' and 'I emailed myself congratulations, replied thanks, and forwarded it to everyone!' both edge toward the confession-only truth (lonely, self-generated numbers).

Split test cap: the persona allows one split test per episode, but the bank carries three A/B lines that could be drawn in one episode ('Variant A: you're stunning...', 'Variant A: I compliment the coat...', 'Two first dates, same night, two restaurants...').
